title: USGS publishes more than one count of active volcanoes
summary: The USGS volcano FAQ says about 1,350 potentially active volcanoes. A 2016 article quoted on the same page says about 1,550. Another passage counts eruptions in 10,000 years.
body: The U.S. Geological Survey FAQ "How many active volcanoes are there on Earth?" answers that there are about 1,350 potentially active volcanoes worldwide, aside from the continuous belts on the ocean floor at spreading centers, and that about 500 of those 1,350 have erupted in historical time. The same fetched page quotes a 2 August 2016 USGS article that says there are approximately 1,550 potentially active volcanoes. Another passage on the page says more than 1,500 volcanoes have erupted in the past 10,000 years. The page does not reconcile the figures. They are different wordings, and "potentially active," "erupted in historical time," and "erupted in the past 10,000 years" are not the same set. The page also says about 170 potentially active volcanoes in the United States and its territories, and a video caption on the page says the United States has 169 active volcanoes.
